question.problem:
What is the first term that exceeds $58\,000$ in the following geometric sequence?

$$
2,\,8,\,32,\,128,\,…
$$

The first term that exceeds $58\,000$ is the
{{field-1}}th term.
question.worked_solution:
The first term of the sequence is ${a}_{1}=2$ and the common ratio is

$$
r=\frac{8}{2}=4.
$$

So, the $n$th term of the sequence can be written as

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{n} & ={a}_{1}\cdot {r}^{n-1} \\  & =2\cdot {4}^{n-1}.\end{aligned}
$$

We want the $n$th term to be greater than $58\,000.$
Hence,

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{n} & >58\,000 \\ 2\cdot {4}^{n-1} & >58\,000 \\ {4}^{n-1} & >29\,000 \\ \operatorname{log}⁡({4}^{n-1}) & >\operatorname{log}⁡(29\,000) \\ (n-1)\operatorname{log}⁡(4) & >\operatorname{log}⁡(29\,000) \\ n-1 & >\frac{\operatorname{log}⁡(29\,000)}{\operatorname{log}⁡(4)} \\ n & >\frac{\operatorname{log}⁡(29\,000)}{\operatorname{log}⁡(4)}+1.\end{aligned}
$$

Estimating the right-hand side using a calculator, we get

$$
\frac{\operatorname{log}⁡(29\,000)}{\operatorname{log}⁡(4)}+1≈8.412.
$$

Therefore, the $9$th term is the first term of the sequence that exceeds $58\,000.$
